# Multi-Tenant Document Store REST API

I'll design this around proven patterns — standard REST conventions win because they're boring and everyone knows them.

## Resources & Structure

```
Documents (the core resource)
  GET    /v1/documents                    List documents in tenant
  POST   /v1/documents                    Create document
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}               Fetch document
  PUT    /v1/documents/{id}               Replace document
  PATCH  /v1/documents/{id}               Partial update
  DELETE /v1/documents/{id}               Delete document
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions      Version history
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions/{v}  Fetch specific version

Tenants (manage team/workspace)
  GET    /v1/tenants/{id}                 Fetch tenant info
  PUT    /v1/tenants/{id}                 Update tenant settings

Users (within tenant)
  GET    /v1/tenants/{id}/users           List users
  POST   /v1/tenants/{id}/users           Invite user
```

## Authentication Model

**Bearer token + tenant isolation (no tenant ID in URL—it's implicit from token):**

```
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_or_opaque_token}
X-Tenant-ID: {tenant_id}  # Optional, strict validation against token
```

**Why:** Token contains tenant scope; tenant ID is a safety check. One request identifies both who and which tenant. Standard JWT payload:

```json
{
  "sub": "user_id",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "scopes": ["documents:read", "documents:write"],
  "exp": 1234567890
}
```

**Enforce at middleware:** Every request validates token exists, extract tenant_id, reject if it drifts. Tenant ID is not part of the URL, it's implicit—prevents accidental cross-tenant queries.

## Pagination

**Limit/offset with cursor support optional later:**

```
GET /v1/documents?limit=50&offset=100

Response:
{
  "data": [...],
  "pagination": {
    "limit": 50,
    "offset": 100,
    "total": 5000,
    "has_more": true
  }
}
```

**Why:** Limit/offset is simpler to implement, reason about, and client-side. Cursor-based is better at scale (offset becomes expensive with large datasets), but add it when you measure that problem. Default limit=20, max=500.

## Versioning

**URI versioning (/v1/, /v2/):**

```
GET /v1/documents        # Current stable
GET /v2/documents        # New version
```

**Why:** Dead simple. Header-based versioning (`Accept-Version: 2`) looks elegant but creates routing chaos—URL versioning forces clean breaking changes and forces clients to pick a version explicitly. Boring wins.

Deprecation via headers:

```
Deprecation: true
Sunset: Wed, 21 Nov 2026 00:00:00 GMT
Link: <https://api.example.com/v2/docs>; rel="successor-version"
```

## Error Format

**RFC 7807 Problem Details (but keep it minimal):**

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/validation-error",
  "status": 422,
  "title": "Validation Failed",
  "detail": "The request body has 2 validation errors",
  "instance": "/v1/documents",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "title",
      "message": "Title is required"
    },
    {
      "field": "content",
      "message": "Content must be at least 1 character"
    }
  ]
}
```

Standard codes:

| Status | Use |
|--------|-----|
| **400** | Bad request (malformed JSON, invalid params) |
| **401** | Missing/invalid auth token |
| **403** | Tenant mismatch or insufficient scopes |
| **404** | Document not found |
| **409** | Conflict (duplicate key, version mismatch) |
| **422** | Validation failed |
| **429** | Rate limited |
| **500** | Server error |

## Document Structure

```json
{
  "id": "doc_abc123",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_456",
  "title": "My Doc",
  "content": "...",
  "created_at": "2026-11-06T14:22:30Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-06T14:22:30Z",
  "created_by": "user_789",
  "version": 3,
  "etag": "\"33a64df551\"",
  "metadata": {
    "tags": ["draft"],
    "owner": "user_789"
  }
}
```

**ETag for concurrency:** Include `ETag` header and check `If-Match` on updates. Prevents overwriting concurrent edits. No timestamp-based concurrency, ETags are simpler.

## Key Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| **Tenant ID in token, not URL** | Simplifies routing, forces tenant validation at auth layer. URL stays clean. |
| **Limit/offset pagination** | Ships now. Cursor-based is premature optimization. |
| **URI versioning** | Explicit, forces breaking-change discipline, standard industry practice. |
| **RFC 7807 errors** | Standard format, clients recognize it. Lightweight subset (not every edge case). |
| **ETag for concurrency** | Avoids timestamp skew issues, works offline. Simpler than version numbers in payload. |
| **Bearer token auth** | Industry standard. JWTs are optional (opaque tokens work too). |
| **Scopes in token** | Fine-grained per-user access without extra lookups. Check scopes at middleware. |

**Skipped:** Custom API key schemes (Bearer is standard), hypermedia (REST Level 3 adds routing complexity, rarely used), webhook versioning (keep webhooks simple—version the event payload only).

Ship this. Complexity arrives when you have real load or scale problems, not before.
